subject: [PATCH v2 09/12] mm/collapse: open-code collapse_single_pmd() in its two callers

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about locking expectations in collapse_single_pmd() by explaining that the split puts the boundary where the lock is, making it easier to move the scan to per-VMA locking.
reviews.raw_body:
I gave more motivation in my reply to David:

https://lore.kernel.org/all/aqQf9hSy0iNjnL6t@thinkstation/

Short version: scan and run have different locking expectations, and
the split puts the boundary where the lock is. It is also what makes
moving the scan to per-VMA locking trivial, since the caller owns the
lock and the engine never touches it.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

2026-09-14.patch_summary: This patch removes the collapse_single_pmd() function and instead open-codes it in its two callers, khugepaged's walk and madvise_collapse(). The function is responsible for collapsing a single PMD by scanning under the lock held by the caller and then giving up the lock before running the collapse. The patch maintains the same locking behavior as before and does not introduce any functional changes.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan noted that despite the patch's goal to minimize code divergence between madvise_collapse and khugepaged, the two workflows are incompatible due to their differing locking requirements.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks. You also explained this to me in my early email to patch 9.
It makes sense.

My motivation is to minimize code divergence of madvise_collapse and khugepaged.
But it seems that their workflows prevent the unification.

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi
